transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh, yeah… I came in because I’m just not sleeping right anymore. Like, I’ll lay there for hours and if I hear rain, or even just start thinking about the bluff giving way, my brain won’t shut up. 

And then when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up all sweaty from dreams, and it’s like I never slept at all. I work at a call center, and I’ll be sitting there trying to sound normal to people complaining about bills or whatever, but I’m just exhausted. It’s been messing me up.
You mentioned the bluff giving way, is that something that happened to you or someone you know?

I mean… yeah, the bluff thing is what’s been stuck in my head, but I don’t really know how to explain it right. It wasn’t like… I don’t know. I keep picturing it, and then I start thinking about rain and how the ground gets all soft, and it’s weird because at work there’s this one guy who always talks about mudslides like he’s some kind of weather expert, and it makes me want to just leave the room.

But, uh… sorry, what were you asking exactly? If it happened to me or someone I know? I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly.
Did something happen to you or someone you know that involved a bluff giving way?

I… I don’t know if I can say it like that. Like, something happened, yeah, or I think that’s why my head keeps going back to it, but when you say “to me or someone I know,” I get kind of stuck.

It’s not like I have a clean little story ready. I just keep getting pieces of it in my head, and then I’m thinking about the hill behind this old place near where I used to hang out, and how people always say “oh, it’s probably fine,” but they don’t really know, you know? And then I start thinking about how dumb it is that they build stuff so close to edges anyway.

Sorry… I’m not really answering right. I’m not sure how to explain what happened.
Did something bad or frightening happen to you or someone else that involved a bluff or a hill?

Yeah… yeah, something bad happened. I got trapped after this bluff trail collapsed. It was about four months ago now, I think. 

It’s weird, because I keep thinking about little stuff from that day, like the dirt and how trails never look dangerous until they do, and people just keep walking on them like it’s nothing. But… yeah, that’s when all this started. Four months ago.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations because they remind you of what happened on the bluff trail?

Yeah… I do. I won’t go near the coast trails anymore. Like, even if someone says it’s a different trail or it’s safe or whatever, I just… I don’t want to be anywhere near that kind of edge.

And my hiking buddies still text sometimes, like asking if I’m coming out, or sending pictures of where they’re going, and I’ll just leave it unread or say I’m busy. Even just talking about going back out there makes my chest get tight. It’s stupid because I used to like that stuff, and now I’m making excuses like I have errands or work, even when I don’t.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the bluff trail collapse, like it's happening all over again?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like I’m literally there, I know I’m not, but it hits weird.

I’ll be at work, just sitting at my desk with the headset on, and out of nowhere I hear it in my head — like rocks sliding, that scraping sound — and then I’m thinking about my leg being stuck under me. For a minute it’s like I’m back on that trail instead of in the call center. And then someone’s asking me about their account or whatever and I’m just… trying to sound normal.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened on the bluff trail?

Yeah, I mean… I try not to let myself go there. If it starts coming up, I’ll do something else or change the subject.

Like, I won’t even go near the coast trails now, and when my hiking buddies text me, I kind of dodge it. I’ll leave it sitting there or say I’m busy, because even just talking about going out there makes my chest tighten. And then I end up thinking about dumb stuff instead, like work schedules or what I need from the store, anything else really.
Do you often find yourself easily startled by small things?

I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that, I guess. Like, small things? Maybe if someone drops something I look over, but I think everybody does that.

At work there’s always noise too, phones ringing and people talking over each other, so it’s kind of hard to tell what’s me being jumpy and what’s just, you know, that place being loud. I’ve been meaning to ask if they can move my station actually, because the guy next to me taps his pen all day and it drives me nuts—but yeah, startled? I’m not sure.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened on the bluff trail?

Yeah… I do. I keep thinking I was stupid for going out there by myself. Like, who does that, you know? I should’ve paid more attention, or turned around, or… I don’t know.

And then I’ll get stuck on that for a while, like I was careless and basically caused it somehow. My mom says stuff like “you couldn’t have known,” but it doesn’t really land. Now even in normal places I feel like if I’m not watching everything, something bad’s gonna happen. Like if I relax for one second, that’s when it’ll go wrong.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do some stuff, just… not always the same way, I guess. Like I used to mess around with games after work, and sometimes I still turn them on, but then I end up scrolling on my phone instead.

But I don’t know if that’s “lost interest” or just being tired. Work’s been weird too—people keep quitting, so the schedule changes, and then I get home and it’s like, do I want to do anything or just sit there? I guess I haven’t really thought about it like that.
Has what's been happening since the bluff trail collapse affected your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, kind of. Not always in, like, a big dramatic way, but I’ve been avoiding some people. Especially the people I used to hike with. They’ll text me stuff like, “We should all get together,” and I just… don’t answer right away, or I make up some excuse.

And then with family, it’s more like I’m tired all the time, so I’m not really talking much. My mom keeps asking if I’m studying for my GED, and I say I am, but I’ve fallen behind. I keep thinking I’ll do it after work, but then I just can’t get myself to focus.

Work’s been bad too—sorry, I know you asked about friends and family, but it all kind of runs together. I missed some important CRM notes on a call, and it turned into an escalation, and I got written up. I was trying to move toward team lead eventually, and now I feel like I probably messed that up. So then I don’t want to talk to anyone because I’m embarrassed, and it just turns into me staying by myself more.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

I don’t know… I feel like I kind of answered that badly before. It’s hard to tell if I’ve lost interest or if I just get distracted or tired.

Like, I’ll think I want to play something or watch a show, and then I just end up not really doing it. But then sometimes I do still enjoy it a little, so I don’t know if that counts. It’s not like I woke up and was like, “I hate everything I used to like.” It’s more just… things don’t stick the same way, I guess.
Have you felt like your daily life or work has been significantly impacted by what's been going on since the bluff trail collapse?

Yeah… I think it has. Work especially. Like, I’ve always had annoying calls, you know, people yelling about billing or whatever, and usually I can just type the notes and move on. But lately I missed some important CRM notes after a call, and it turned into this whole escalation, and then I got written up.

And I keep thinking about it because I was trying to maybe move toward team lead eventually, or at least not look like I’m barely keeping up, and now it feels like I might’ve ruined that. So then I get home and I’m supposed to study for my GED, but I’m just exhausted and I put it off.

And socially too, I guess. I don’t really answer the hiking group much anymore. They’ll text and I just kind of avoid it, then feel weird about avoiding it. So yeah, it’s not like my whole life stopped, but it’s definitely messing things up.
How often do you find yourself avoiding places or activities that remind you of the bluff trail collapse?

Pretty often, yeah. I mean, I don’t go near the coast trails at all now. Even if someone mentions a walk out that way, I’m like, no, I can’t do that.

And my hiking buddies still text sometimes, and I’ll see the message and just leave it there. Not even because I’m mad at them or anything. It’s just that even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten, and then I start thinking about the whole thing, so I dodge it.
Do you avoid reminders of the bluff trail collapse every day?

Not every single day, I don’t think… I mean, it depends what comes up. Like if I’m just working and nobody says anything about hiking or the coast, maybe I don’t have to avoid it directly.

But I won’t go near the coast trails now at all. And when my hiking buddies text, I dodge it a lot, because even just talking about going out there makes my chest get tight. Then I’m like, okay, I’ll answer later, and then I just don’t. So… not every day maybe, but pretty often.
